full_judgment:
4. Both the trial Court and the lower Appellate Court held that the order of the Government allowing the respondents to hold the charge of Superintendents with the designation of Clerk-in-Charge amounted to promotion, that by virtue of the Memo No. MF(IC)-2/73/3, dated 21st March 1974 they are entitled to have their pay fixed in Grade No.VI and on this finding decreed the suit. In second appeal-S.A.No.421 of 1979-a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division maintained the decree with a modification that though the respondents are entitled to have their pay fixed in Grade No.VI, yet by mere holding the charge for over six months they did not stand promoted. 

 7. Having considered all aspects of the matter we find that the High Court Division maintained the decree of the lower Courts by correctly applying the Memorandum in question in the case of the respondents. In the result, the appeal is dismissed, without however, any order as to costs.
